1	# Real-world Event Decision Simulator
2	
3	A small backend foundation for an emergency-response and logistics decision simulation platform. The service exposes a public HTTP entry point that future features can extend without changing the startup contract.
4	
5	## Run
6	
7	Requires Python 3.11 or newer and has no third-party runtime dependencies.
8	
9	```bash
10	python -m event_sim serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8000
11	```
12	
13	Check the public health endpoint:
14	
15	```bash
16	curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/health
17	```
18	
19	## Test
20	
21	```bash
22	python -m unittest discover -s tests -v
23	```
24	
25	## Public interface
26	
27	- `GET /health` returns JSON with the service name and `ok` status, under the keys `service` and `status`: `{"service": "real-world-event-decision-sim", "status": "ok"}`.
28	- Unknown paths return a JSON `not_found` error with HTTP 404.
29	- `python -m event_sim --help` documents the command-line entry point.
30	
31	## Credentials and organization isolation
32	
33	Every entry point except `GET /health` and the credential registration entry
34	point requires a request-scoped Bearer credential. Credentials are held only
35	in the server process: restarting (or starting a new instance) begins with an
36	empty credential registry, and an unregistered token reaches nothing.
37	
38	### `POST /auth/tokens`
39	
40	The one entry point that requires no credential. Requires
41	`Content-Type: application/json`. The body must be a JSON object with exactly
42	these three fields, in any order:
43	
44	| Field            | Rule                                  |
45	| ---------------- | ------------------------------------- |
46	| `token`          | non-empty string                      |
47	| `organizationId` | non-empty string                      |
48	| `role`           | one of `read` or `write`              |
49	
50	- `201 Created` — new token registered. The body echoes the three fields as
51	  compact JSON with keys sorted by code point and one trailing newline:
52	  `{"organizationId":"org-1","role":"write","token":"tok-1"}\n`.
53	- `200 OK` — the same token was resubmitted with the identical organization
54	  and role; it is not registered a second time and the same body is echoed.
55	- `409 Conflict` (`{"error": "auth_conflict"}`) — the token is already bound
56	  to a different organization or role. The binding is never rewritten.
57	- `415 Unsupported Media Type` — missing or unsupported `Content-Type`.
58	- `400 Bad Request` — body is not syntactically valid JSON.
59	- `422 Unprocessable Entity` (`validation_error`) — a non-object body, a
60	  missing/extra field, a blank or non-string `token`/`organizationId`, or a
61	  `role` other than `read`/`write`. No record is stored.
62	
63	```bash
64	curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/auth/tokens \
65	  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
66	  -d '{"token":"tok-1","organizationId":"org-1","role":"write"}'
67	```
68	
69	### Bearer authentication
70	
71	All other requests carry the registered token in an
72	`Authorization: Bearer <token>` header. A missing header, a non-Bearer
73	scheme, a malformed bearer value, or an unregistered token yields
74	`401 Unauthorized` with `{"error": "unauthorized"}`.
75	
76	A valid credential that acts outside its bound organization or role yields
77	`403 Forbidden` with `{"error": "forbidden"}` and performs no write. The
78	`organizationId` in any request parameter or body field must equal the
79	token's registered organization; reading or writing another organization's
80	data is forbidden.
81	
82	- A `read` token may call only the state-free query and decision-computation
83	  entry points: the event list, aggregate, region, and replay (including
84	  replay comparison) queries, the reservation/alert listings,
85	  `GET /branches/{branchId}/resources`,
86	  `POST /decisions/evaluate`, `POST /decisions/allocate`,
87	  `POST /branches/compare`, `POST /branches/compare/events`,
88	  `POST /branches/compare/reservations`,
89	  `POST /branches/compare/resources`, `POST /snapshots/compare`,
90	  `POST /snapshots/compare/events`,
91	  `POST /snapshots/compare/reservations`,
92	  `POST /snapshots/compare/resources`, and the other
93	  read-only branch entry points.
94	- Committing an event or reservation, evaluating an alert, and creating a
95	  snapshot or branch are writes; only a `write` token may call them. A
96	  `read` token against a write entry point receives `403`. The authorization
97	  decision and the ledger/inventory mutation complete under one lock, so a
98	  rejected request never changes the ledger or inventory.
99	
100	Snapshots and branches belong to the organization that created them. A
101	snapshot captures only that organization's events, resource capacities, and
102	reservations, and the three summary counts count only that organization; a
103	branch forks only a snapshot owned by the same organization, and branch entry
104	points authenticate with the same rules as the main service. Snapshot and
105	branch names are unique across the whole service (not merely within one
106	organization), and accessing another organization's snapshot or branch by name
107	is `403`, never `404`.
108	
109	## Event ledger
110	
111	Events are held only in the server process: restarting (or starting a new
112	instance) begins with an empty ledger.
113	
114	### `POST /events`
115	
116	Requires `Content-Type: application/json`. The body must be a JSON object with
117	exactly these five top-level fields:
118	
119	| Field          | Rule                                      |
120	| -------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
121	| `eventId`      | non-empty string                          |
122	| `organizationId` | non-empty string                        |
123	| `type`         | non-empty string                          |
124	| `occurredAt`   | non-negative integer (no floats, no booleans) |
125	| `payload`      | JSON object                               |
126	
127	```bash
128	curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/events \
129	  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
130	  -d '{"eventId":"evt-1","organizationId":"org-1","type":"incident.created","occurredAt":100,"payload":{"severity":"low"}}'
131	```
132	
133	- `201 Created` — new event stored; the response is the same five-field JSON.
134	- `200 OK` — the same `eventId` was resubmitted with identical fields; the
135	  stored event is returned and nothing is added.
136	- `409 Conflict` (`{"error": "event_id_conflict"}`) — the `eventId` exists but
137	  the other fields differ.
138	- `415 Unsupported Media Type` — missing or unsupported `Content-Type`.
139	- `400 Bad Request` — body is not syntactically valid JSON.
140	- `422 Unprocessable Entity` — fields are missing, extra, or invalid
141	  (arrays at the top level, blank identifiers, floats, etc.).
142	
143	### `GET /events?organizationId=...`
144	
145	The `organizationId` query parameter must appear exactly once and be non-empty.
146	Returns `200` with `{"organizationId": "...", "events": [...]}`, where events
147	belong only to that organization and are sorted by `occurredAt`, then
148	`eventId`. An unknown organization returns `"events": []`. A missing, blank, or
149	duplicated parameter yields `422`.
150	
151	### `GET /events/aggregate?organizationId=...&type=...&windowSize=...`
152	
153	Counts stored events per time window, without modifying the ledger. Only
154	events matching both `organizationId` and `type` are counted; other
155	organizations' data is never included.
156	
157	Query parameters:
158	
159	| Parameter        | Rule                                                                 |
160	| ---------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------- |
161	| `organizationId` | required exactly once, non-empty string                              |
162	| `type`           | required exactly once, non-empty string                              |
163	| `windowSize`     | required exactly once, positive integer text (e.g. `60`)             |
164	| `from`           | optional; non-negative integer text, exactly once if present         |
165	| `to`             | optional; non-negative integer text, exactly once if present         |
166	
167	`from` and `to` must be omitted together or supplied together, and must
168	satisfy `from <= to`. A missing, duplicated, or invalid parameter yields
169	`422` with a JSON body containing a stable `error` field.
170	
171	Windows start at `0` and each covers `[start, end)` with
172	`end = start + windowSize`; an event belongs to a window when
173	`start <= occurredAt < end`. The `200` response is:
174	
175	```json
176	{
177	  "organizationId": "org-1",
178	  "type": "incident.created",
179	  "windowSize": 60,
180	  "from": null,
181	  "to": null,
182	  "windows": [{"start": 0, "end": 60, "count": 2}]
183	}
184	```
185	
186	- Without `from`/`to` (`from` and `to` echo back as `null`), only windows
187	  actually covered by matching events are returned; with no matching events
188	  `windows` is `[]`.
189	- With `from`/`to`, only events with `from <= occurredAt <= to` are counted,
190	  and every window intersecting the closed interval `[from, to]` is returned,
191	  including empty windows with `count: 0`.
192	- `windows` is sorted by `start` ascending; results are deterministic
193	  regardless of event insertion order, replays, or identical timestamps.
194	
195	```bash
196	curl 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/events/aggregate?organizationId=org-1&type=incident.created&windowSize=60&from=0&to=180'
197	```
198	
199	### Region attribution
200	
201	An event's region is the value of the `region` key in its `payload`. Only a
202	non-empty string attributes an event to a region: a missing key, an empty
203	string, or a non-string value means the event has no region. Region values
204	are matched verbatim (exact comparison, no trimming or normalization), and
205	regions need no registration — an unknown region simply matches zero events
206	and is never implicitly created. The region endpoints below are read-only:
207	they never write the event ledger, reservations, or alerts.
208	
209	### `GET /events/region?organizationId=...&region=...`
210	
211	Lists one organization's events attributed to one region. Both
212	`organizationId` and `region` must appear exactly once and be non-empty; a
213	missing, duplicated, or blank parameter yields `422`. Returns `200` with
214	`{"organizationId": "...", "region": "...", "events": [...]}`, where events
215	are sorted by `occurredAt`, then `eventId`, exactly like `GET /events`. An
216	unknown organization or region returns `"events": []`; other organizations'
217	events are never included. The body is compact JSON with keys sorted by code
218	point and a trailing newline.
219	
220	```bash
221	curl 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/events/region?organizationId=org-1&region=north'
222	```
223	
224	### `GET /events/region/aggregate?organizationId=...&region=...&type=...&windowSize=...`
225	
226	Counts per time window, using the exact same parameter rules, window
227	boundaries, ordering, and `from`/`to` semantics as
228	`GET /events/aggregate`, with an added `region` parameter that must appear
229	exactly once and be non-empty. Only events matching the organization,
230	region, and type are counted; events without a non-empty string payload
231	`region` never match. The `200` response mirrors the aggregate response with
232	one added `region` key (compact JSON, keys sorted by code point, trailing
233	newline):
234	
235	```json
236	{
237	  "organizationId": "org-1",
238	  "region": "north",
239	  "type": "incident.created",
240	  "windowSize": 60,
241	  "from": null,
242	  "to": null,
243	  "windows": [{"start": 0, "end": 60, "count": 2}]
244	}
245	```
246	
247	Without a range, only windows covered by matching events are returned; an
248	unknown region behaves like a zero-event match. With a range, every window
249	intersecting `[from, to]` is returned, including empty ones. Any parameter
250	problem — missing, duplicated, or blank values, a non-positive-integer
251	`windowSize`, unpaired or non-integer `from`/`to`, or `from > to` — yields
252	`422` with `{"error": "validation_error", ...}`.
253	
254	```bash
255	curl 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/events/region/aggregate?organizationId=org-1&region=north&type=incident.created&windowSize=60&from=0&to=180'
256	```
257	
258	### `POST /decisions/evaluate`
259	
260	A read-only, deterministic emergency decision over the same windows as the
261	aggregate endpoint. The ledger is never written to or changed by a decision
262	request. Requires `Content-Type: application/json`. The body must be a JSON
263	object containing exactly these fields:
264	
265	| Field            | Rule                                                          |
266	| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
267	| `organizationId` | required, non-empty string                                   |
268	| `type`           | required, non-empty string                                   |
269	| `windowSize`     | required, positive integer (no booleans, floats, or strings) |
270	| `threshold`      | required, positive integer (no booleans, floats, or strings) |
271	| `from`           | optional; non-negative integer, present only together with `to` |
272	| `to`             | optional; non-negative integer, present only together with `from` |
273	
274	Only events matching both `organizationId` and `type` are counted. Windows
275	start at `0` and cover `[start, start + windowSize)`. Without `from`/`to`,
276	only windows actually covered by matching events are considered; with a
277	range, events are filtered by the closed interval `from <= occurredAt <= to`
278	and every window intersecting that interval is considered, including empty
279	ones for audit reconciliation.
280	
281	The `200` response has a fixed shape:
282	
283	```json
284	{
285	  "organizationId": "org-1",
286	  "type": "incident.created",
287	  "windowSize": 60,
288	  "from": null,
289	  "to": null,
290	  "peakStart": 60,
291	  "peakCount": 2,
292	  "action": "observe"
293	}
294	```
295	
296	- `peakCount` is the largest window count and `peakStart` is that window's
297	  start; ties resolve to the earliest start, so results are reproducible
298	  regardless of event submission order.
299	- With no matching events (or no non-empty windows in range), `peakCount` is
300	  `0`, `peakStart` is `null`, and `action` is `"observe"`.
301	- `action` is `"escalate"` when `peakCount >= threshold`, otherwise
302	  `"observe"`.
303	- Unknown organizations or types compute as zero events and return normally;
304	  other organizations' data is never included.
305	
306	```bash
307	curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/decisions/evaluate \
308	  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
309	  -d '{"organizationId":"org-1","type":"incident.created","windowSize":60,"threshold":3}'
310	```
311	
312	- `415 Unsupported Media Type` — missing or unsupported `Content-Type`.
313	- `400 Bad Request` — body is not syntactically valid JSON; no decision is
314	  produced.
315	- `422 Unprocessable Entity` — a non-object body, missing or extra fields,
316	  invalid types, unpaired `from`/`to`, or out-of-range values.
317	
318	### `POST /decisions/allocate`
319	
320	A read-only, deterministic resource plan computed entirely from the request
321	body. Nothing is written to the event ledger, no earlier plan is inherited,
322	and concurrent requests cannot affect each other. Requires
323	`Content-Type: application/json`. The body must be a JSON object containing
324	exactly these fields:
325	
326	| Field            | Rule                                                          |
327	| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
328	| `organizationId` | required, non-empty string                                   |
329	| `demands`        | required array (may be empty) of demand objects              |
330	| `resources`      | required array (may be empty) of resource objects            |
331	
332	A demand object has exactly `demandId` (non-empty string, unique within the
333	request), `units` (positive integer), and `priority` (non-negative integer).
334	A resource object has exactly `resourceId` (non-empty string, unique within
335	the request) and `capacity` (positive integer). Booleans, floats, negative or
336	zero values where a positive integer is required, wrong element types, blank
337	or duplicate identifiers, and unknown fields are all rejected.
338	
339	Demands are handled by `priority` descending; ties resolve by `demandId` in
340	Unicode code-point order. A demand is placed wholly into the
341	lexicographically smallest `resourceId` whose remaining capacity covers its
342	units, and that capacity is deducted immediately. Demands are never split and
343	capacity is never oversold; a demand that fits in no remaining resource goes
344	to `unassigned` — priorities and units are never adjusted to place more
345	demands.
346	
347	The `200` response has a fixed shape:
348	
349	```json
350	{
351	  "organizationId": "org-1",
352	  "assignments": [
353	    {"demandId": "d-a", "resourceId": "r-a", "units": 2},
354	    {"demandId": "d-b", "resourceId": "r-b", "units": 4}
355	  ],
356	  "unassigned": ["d-big"],
357	  "totalUnits": 6
358	}
359	```
360	
361	- `assignments` lists `{"demandId", "resourceId", "units"}` objects in
362	  processing order.
363	- `unassigned` lists the demandIds that could not be placed, sorted by
364	  `demandId`.
365	- `totalUnits` counts only units that were assigned.
366	- Empty `demands`/`resources` arrays are valid and return empty results;
367	  identical submissions return byte-for-byte identical JSON.
368	
369	```bash
370	curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/decisions/allocate \
371	  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
372	  -d '{"organizationId":"org-1","demands":[{"demandId":"d-a","units":2,"priority":1}],"resources":[{"resourceId":"r-a","capacity":5}]}'
373	```
374	
375	- `415 Unsupported Media Type` — missing or unsupported `Content-Type`.
376	- `400 Bad Request` — body is not syntactically valid JSON.
377	- `422 Unprocessable Entity` — a non-object body, missing or extra fields,
378	  invalid types, duplicate or blank identifiers, or out-of-range values.
379	
380	## Reservation inventory
381	
382	Reservations are held only in the server process alongside the event ledger:
383	restarting (or starting a new instance) begins with empty inventory. The
384	first reservation that names a resource fixes that resource's capacity; it
385	is never rewritten afterwards.
386	
387	### `POST /reservations`
388	
389	Requires `Content-Type: application/json`. The body must be a JSON object
390	with exactly these five top-level fields:
391	
392	| Field           | Rule                                      |
393	| --------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
394	| `organizationId` | non-empty string                         |
395	| `reservationId` | non-empty string                          |
396	| `resourceId`    | non-empty string                          |
397	| `quantity`      | positive integer (no floats, no booleans) |
398	| `capacity`      | positive integer (no floats, no booleans) |
399	
400	```bash
401	curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/reservations \
402	  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
403	  -d '{"organizationId":"org-1","reservationId":"res-1","resourceId":"r-a","quantity":2,"capacity":5}'
404	```
405	
406	A successful response is compact JSON with stable key order, integer values,
407	and a trailing newline:
408	
409	```json
410	{"capacity":5,"occupied":2,"organizationId":"org-1","quantity":2,"remaining":3,"reservationId":"res-1","resourceId":"r-a"}
411	```
412	
413	`occupied` is the total confirmed quantity on the resource and `remaining`
414	is `capacity - occupied`; the balance can never go negative because the
415	check and the deduction commit atomically under one lock, so concurrent
416	requests cannot oversell a resource or lose each other's writes.
417	
418	- `201 Created` — new reservation committed; the first reservation for a
419	  resource also establishes its capacity.
420	- `200 OK` — the same `reservationId` was resubmitted with identical fields;
421	  nothing is counted twice and the balances are unchanged.
422	- `409 Conflict` (`{"error": "reservation_conflict"}`) — the `reservationId`
423	  exists but the other fields differ.
424	- `409 Conflict` (`{"error": "capacity_conflict"}`) — the resource already
425	  has a recorded capacity and the declared `capacity` differs; the recorded
426	  capacity is never rewritten.
427	- `409 Conflict` (`{"error": "capacity_exceeded"}`) — the quantity exceeds
428	  the resource's remaining balance; inventory and existing reservations are
429	  unchanged.
430	- `415 Unsupported Media Type` — missing or unsupported `Content-Type`.
431	- `400 Bad Request` — body is not syntactically valid JSON; no reservation
432	  is produced.
433	- `422 Unprocessable Entity` — a non-object body, missing or extra fields,
434	  blank or non-string identifiers, or non-positive/non-integer values.
435	
436	### `GET /reservations?organizationId=...`
437	
438	The `organizationId` query parameter must appear exactly once and be
439	non-empty. Returns `200` with `{"organizationId": "...", "reservations":
440	[...]}` containing only that organization's reservations, sorted by
441	`resourceId` then `reservationId` in Unicode code-point order. Each entry
442	carries `quantity`, the resource's `capacity`, and the resource-wide
443	`occupied` and `remaining` balances. An unknown organization returns
444	`"reservations": []`. A missing, blank, or duplicated parameter yields
445	`422`.
446	
447	## Alert suppression and escalation
448	
449	Alerts are held only in the main service process alongside the event
450	ledger; restarting (or starting a new instance) begins with no alerts.
451	Snapshots and branches never capture alerts, and the alert entry points
452	exist only on the main service — no `/branches/{branchId}/alerts/...`
453	paths are added.
454	
455	### `POST /alerts/evaluate`
456	
457	Requires `Content-Type: application/json`. The body must be a JSON object
458	containing exactly these fields:
459	
460	| Field               | Rule                                                          |
461	| ------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
462	| `organizationId`    | required, non-empty string                                   |
463	| `type`              | required, non-empty string                                   |
464	| `windowSize`        | required, positive integer (no booleans, floats, or strings) |
465	| `threshold`         | required, positive integer (no booleans, floats, or strings) |
466	| `suppressionWindow` | required, positive integer (no booleans, floats, or strings) |
467	| `from`              | optional; non-negative integer, present only together with `to` |
468	| `to`                | optional; non-negative integer, present only together with `from` |
469	
470	The peak uses the exact same windowing as `POST /decisions/evaluate`: only
471	events matching both `organizationId` and `type` are counted, windows
472	start at `0` and cover `[start, start + windowSize)`, ties resolve to the
473	earliest window start, and an unknown organization or type computes as
474	zero events. The event ledger is never modified.
475	
476	- When the peak is below the threshold, `action` is `"observe"`, no alert
477	  is written, `alertId` is `null`, and `suppressedCount` is `null`.
478	- When the peak reaches the threshold, the peak start is compared with the
479	  most recent prior alert for the same organization and type:
480	  - `peakStart` not earlier than the prior start and at least
481	    `suppressionWindow` away (`peakStart - priorStart >=
482	    suppressionWindow`) creates a new alert; `action` is `"escalate"`,
483	    `alertId` is the new id (`alert-1`, `alert-2`, …, one global sequence
484	    across all organizations and types), and `suppressedCount` is `0`.
485	  - A peak start less than `suppressionWindow` after the prior alert's
486	    peak start increments that alert's suppression count instead; `action`
487	    is `"suppress"`, `alertId` is the prior alert's id, and
488	    `suppressedCount` is the new total. The first threshold hit for an
489	    organization/type always creates an alert.
490	
491	The suppression decision and the alert creation commit atomically under
492	one lock, so concurrent threshold hits cannot both open alerts or suppress
493	against a stale view. The `200` response echoes every request parameter
494	and adds the result fields (compact JSON, stable key order, integer values,
495	trailing newline):
496	
497	```json
498	{"action":"escalate","alertId":"alert-1","from":null,"organizationId":"org-1","peakCount":3,"peakStart":60,"suppressedCount":0,"suppressionWindow":120,"threshold":3,"to":null,"type":"incident.created","windowSize":60}
499	```
500	
501	```bash
502	curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/alerts/evaluate \
503	  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
504	  -d '{"organizationId":"org-1","type":"incident.created","windowSize":60,"threshold":3,"suppressionWindow":120}'
505	```
506	
507	- `415 Unsupported Media Type` — missing or unsupported `Content-Type`.
508	- `400 Bad Request` — body is not syntactically valid JSON; no alert is
509	  written.
510	- `422 Unprocessable Entity` — a non-object body, missing or extra fields,
511	  blank or non-string identifiers, booleans/floats where integers are
512	  required, non-positive values, unpaired `from`/`to`, or `from > to`.
513	
514	### `GET /alerts?organizationId=...`
515	
516	The `organizationId` query parameter must appear exactly once and be
517	non-empty. Returns `200` with `{"organizationId": "...", "alerts": [...]}`
518	containing only that organization's alerts. Each entry carries `alertId`,
519	`type`, `peakStart`, `threshold`, and `suppressedCount`, sorted by
520	`peakStart` ascending and then `alertId` in Unicode code-point order. An
521	unknown organization returns `"alerts": []`. A missing, blank, or
522	duplicated parameter yields `422`.
523	
524	## Snapshots and branches
525	
526	Snapshots capture the current main service state under a unique name so that
527	decisions can later be recomputed against that exact state. Branches fork a
528	snapshot into an isolated copy that supports the existing event, aggregate,
529	decision, and reservation entry points without sharing any mutable state with
530	the main service or with other branches.
531	
532	### Organization boundaries
533	
534	Every snapshot and branch is owned by the organization of the `write`
535	credential that created it, and all capture, naming, and visibility rules are
536	scoped to that boundary:
537	
538	- A snapshot captures **only the creator's own organization** — its events,
539	  the capacities of resources it reserves, and its reservations. Other
540	  organizations' events, reservation identifiers, and capacity records are
541	  neither captured nor summarized. The three counts in the response
542	  (`events`, `resources`, `reservations`) count only that organization. Two
543	  snapshots created from the same state return identical counts; another
544	  organization's data never changes them.
545	- A branch forked from a snapshot carries only that snapshot organization's
546	  data. Inside the branch, event and reservation names are compared only
547	  against that organization's own records. Another organization's event
548	  identifiers, reservation identifiers, and capacity records never cause a
549	  branch commit to conflict and never affect a branch balance.
550	- Snapshot and branch names are **unique across the whole service** and are
551	  owned by the creator's organization. A duplicate name conflicts regardless
552	  of which organization holds it: creating a snapshot with a name already in
553	  use returns `409` `snapshot_conflict` (the original snapshot is never
554	  rewritten), and creating a branch with a name already in use returns `409`
555	  `branch_conflict` (the existing branch is untouched). Names are not
556	  namespaced per organization.
557	- Using another organization's **snapshot name as a fork source**, or reading
558	  another organization's **branch by name**, returns `403 Forbidden`
559	  (`{"error": "forbidden"}`) with no content, even though the name exists. A
560	  name that has never appeared anywhere is the only case that yields `404`:
561	  a missing snapshot is `snapshot_not_found` and a missing branch is
562	  `branch_not_found`. Missing objects are never implicitly created.
563	- When creating a branch, snapshot ownership (`403`) is decided before the
564	  duplicate branch name (`409`); a foreign snapshot is forbidden even if the
565	  requested `branchId` is also taken. The snapshot list (`GET /snapshots`)
566	  and branch summaries are visible only within the owning organization.
567	- Authorization and the write happen under one lock for alert evaluation,
568	  snapshot creation, and branch creation alike. A rejected request leaves no
569	  alert, snapshot, or branch behind, and concurrent creations of the same
570	  name have exactly one winner; the loser receives the conflict response.
571	
572	Snapshots and branches capture only events, resource capacities, and
573	reservations — alerts are never captured, and the alert entry points remain
574	main-only with no branch-prefixed sub-paths. Like everything else here,
575	snapshots and branches live only in the server process and are cleared on
576	restart; there is no persistence, authorization, or replay across restarts.
577	
578	### `POST /snapshots`
579	
580	Requires a `write` credential and `Content-Type: application/json`. The body
581	must be a JSON object containing exactly one field:
582	
583	| Field        | Rule                     |
584	| ------------ | ------------------------ |
585	| `snapshotId` | non-empty string         |
586	
587	The snapshot is owned by the caller's organization and captures only that
588	organization's state. A successful response is `201` with compact integer
589	JSON:
590	
591	```json
592	{"events":2,"reservations":1,"resources":1,"snapshotId":"snap-1"}
593	```
594	
595	- `events`, `resources`, and `reservations` count the creator organization's
596	  captured events, distinct resources with a recorded capacity, and
597	  reservations; other organizations' data is never counted.
598	- `409 Conflict` (`{"error": "snapshot_conflict"}`) — the name already exists
599	  anywhere in the service (held by any organization); the original snapshot
600	  content is never replaced or mutated.
601	- `403 Forbidden` — the credential is read-only or acts outside its
602	  organization; no snapshot is stored.
603	- `415 Unsupported Media Type` — missing or unsupported `Content-Type`.
604	- `400 Bad Request` — body is not syntactically valid JSON.
605	- `422 Unprocessable Entity` — a non-object body, a missing or extra field,
606	  a blank value, or a non-string `snapshotId`.
607	- Any failed request leaves both the main state and existing snapshots
608	  unchanged.
609	
610	### `GET /snapshots`
611	
612	Returns `200` with `{"snapshots": [...]}`, listing **only the caller
613	organization's** snapshots; other organizations' snapshots are never visible.
614	Each entry has the same shape as a creation response, and entries are sorted
615	by `snapshotId` in Unicode code-point order. With no snapshots the collection
616	is an empty array.
617	
618	### `POST /branches`
619	
620	Requires a `write` credential and `Content-Type: application/json`. The body
621	must be a JSON object containing exactly these fields:
622	
623	| Field        | Rule                     |
624	| ------------ | ------------------------ |
625	| `branchId`   | non-empty string         |
626	| `snapshotId` | non-empty string         |
627	
628	The new branch receives independent copies of the snapshot's events,
629	resource capacities, and reservation balances (which hold only the snapshot
630	owner organization's data).
631	
632	- `201 Created` — the branch summary is returned:
633	
634	```json
635	{"branchId":"br-1","events":2,"reservations":1,"resources":1,"snapshotId":"snap-1"}
636	```
637	
638	- `403 Forbidden` (`{"error": "forbidden"}`) — the named snapshot exists but
639	  belongs to another organization (ownership is checked before the branch
640	  name), or the credential is read-only. No branch is created and no snapshot
641	  content is returned.
642	- `404 Not Found` (`{"error": "snapshot_not_found"}`) — no snapshot with that
643	  name has ever existed; no branch is created.
644	- `409 Conflict` (`{"error": "branch_conflict"}`) — the snapshot is owned by
645	  the caller but a branch with that `branchId` already exists anywhere in the
646	  service. The existing branch is unaffected.
647	- `415`, `400`, and `422` follow the same rules as other JSON write
648	  endpoints; `422` (`validation_error`) covers missing, extra, blank, or
649	  non-string fields.
650	
651	### `GET /branches/{branchId}`
652	
653	Returns `200` with the branch summary (see above) when the branch belongs to
654	the caller's organization. A branch owned by another organization returns
655	`403` with `{"error": "forbidden"}` and no content. Only a branch name that
656	has never existed returns `404` with `{"error": "branch_not_found"}`.
657	
658	### Branch-prefixed entry points
659	
660	A known branch exposes the existing endpoints under
661	`/branches/{branchId}/...`, with identical request contracts, query
662	validation, ordering, and window semantics:
663	
664	| Method | Path                                      | Effect                                    |
665	| ------ | ----------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
666	| GET    | `/branches/{branchId}/events`             | list the branch's events                  |
667	| GET    | `/branches/{branchId}/events/aggregate`   | aggregate the branch's events             |
668	| POST   | `/branches/{branchId}/events`             | commit an event into the branch only      |
669	| POST   | `/branches/{branchId}/decisions/evaluate` | evaluate against the branch's events only |
670	| GET    | `/branches/{branchId}/reservations`       | list the branch's reservations            |
671	| GET    | `/branches/{branchId}/resources`          | list the branch's resource balances       |
672	| POST   | `/branches/{branchId}/reservations`       | reserve against branch balances only      |
673	
674	- Branch event commits honor `415`, `400`, `422`, identical-replay (`200`),
675	  and `event_id_conflict` (`409`); writes stay in the branch. Name and
676	  capacity comparisons run only against the owning organization's records
677	  that were forked into the branch, so another organization's event
678	  identifiers, reservation identifiers, and capacity records never trigger a
679	  conflict and never affect a branch balance.
680	- Branch reservation commits honor `415`, `400`, `422`, and the replay and
681	  capacity rules: identical replays return `200` without double counting,
682	  while `reservation_conflict`, `capacity_conflict`, and
683	  `capacity_exceeded` still return `409`; a failed commit never changes the
684	  branch inventory.
685	- Branch list and aggregate queries apply the same parameter rules as the
686	  main endpoints; missing, duplicated, or empty parameters return `422` with
687	  `validation_error`.
688	- Branch evaluation is read-only over branch events, and branch aggregates
689	  never count main-service events; repeated identical requests return
690	  identical results.
691	- No branch operation creates or rolls back main-service state, and branches
692	  never observe each other's writes. Unknown sub-paths under a known branch
693	  return the standard JSON `404`; sub-paths under an unknown branch return
694	  `branch_not_found`.
695	- The region queries (`/events/region` and `/events/region/aggregate`) are
696	  main-only; no branch-prefixed region paths are added.
697	- `/decisions/allocate` remains a main-only, stateless endpoint.
698	
699	### `GET /branches/{branchId}/resources?organizationId=...`
700	
701	A read-only listing of one branch's current resource balances for the
702	caller's organization — the single-branch counterpart of
703	`POST /branches/compare/resources`, computed from the exact same balance
704	contract. Nothing in the branch, in any other branch, or in the main
705	service is read for mutation or written, alert state is untouched, and
706	identical requests return byte-for-byte identical JSON. Both `read` and
707	`write` credentials may call it. The `organizationId` query parameter
708	must appear exactly once and be non-empty.
709	
710	The `200` response echoes the organization and branch identifiers and
711	carries one row per resource the organization reserves in the branch,
712	sorted by `resourceId` in Unicode code-point order. Each row reports the
713	three balances: `capacity` (fixed by the first reservation naming the
714	resource in the branch), `occupied` (the sum of every reservation the
715	organization holds against the resource in that branch — multiple
716	reservations all count), and `remaining` (`capacity - occupied`).
717	Reservations of other organizations never contribute, and a branch with
718	no resources returns an empty `resources` array. Because the balances
719	share the comparison's contract, comparing a branch with itself via
720	`POST /branches/compare/resources` reports every listed row as `equal`.
721	
722	The response is compact JSON with keys sorted by code point, integer
723	values kept as integers, and one trailing newline:
724	
725	```json
726	{"branchId":"br-1","organizationId":"org-1","resources":[{"capacity":10,"occupied":3,"remaining":7,"resourceId":"res-a"},{"capacity":4,"occupied":1,"remaining":3,"resourceId":"res-b"}]}
727	```
728	
729	```bash
730	curl 'http://127.0.0.1:8000/branches/br-1/resources?organizationId=org-1' \
731	  -H 'Authorization: Bearer tok-1'
732	```
733	
734	The verdict order is fixed: the credential is checked first, then the
735	query shape, then the organization, and only then the branch name.
736	
737	- `401 Unauthorized` (`{"error": "unauthorized"}`) — the Bearer credential
738	  is missing, malformed, or not registered.
739	- `422 Unprocessable Entity` (`validation_error`) — the `organizationId`
740	  parameter is missing, duplicated, or blank.
741	- `403 Forbidden` (`{"error": "forbidden"}`) — the parameter's
742	  organization differs from the credential's, or the named branch belongs
743	  to another organization.
744	- `404 Not Found` (`{"error": "branch_not_found"}`) — the branch name has
745	  never existed; a listing never implicitly creates a branch.
746	
747	Every non-`200` result is read-only as well: a failed request creates no
748	branch and changes no event, reservation, alert, or main-service state.

750	### `POST /branches/compare`
751	
752	A read-only comparison of two existing branches' window counts and peak
753	decisions. Each side recomputes its window counts and peak from that
754	branch's own events only; nothing in either branch, in any other branch, or
755	in the main service is read for mutation or written, and identical
756	submissions return byte-for-byte identical JSON. Both `read` and `write`
757	credentials may call it. Requires `Content-Type: application/json` and a
758	Bearer credential bound to the request's `organizationId`. The body must be
759	a JSON object containing exactly these fields:
760	
761	| Field            | Rule                                                          |
762	| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
763	| `organizationId` | required, non-empty string; both branches must belong to it |
764	| `left`           | required, non-empty branch name (the left-hand side)         |
765	| `right`          | required, non-empty branch name (the right-hand side)        |
766	| `type`           | required, non-empty string                                   |
767	| `windowSize`     | required, positive integer (no booleans, floats, or strings) |
768	| `threshold`      | required, positive integer (no booleans, floats, or strings) |
769	| `from`           | optional; non-negative integer, present only together with `to` |
770	| `to`             | optional; non-negative integer, present only together with `from` |
771	
772	Using the same branch name for `left` and `right` is legal; the two sides
773	are then equal by construction. Window division matches the aggregate and
774	decision entry points exactly: windows start at `0` and cover
775	`[start, start + windowSize)`, and an event counts toward the window of
776	`floor(occurredAt / windowSize) * windowSize`.
777	
778	- Without `from`/`to`, the `windows` rows cover the **union** of the windows
779	  hit by matching events on either side, aligned row-by-row by `start`
780	  ascending. A window hit by only one side shows the other side's count as
781	  `0`. When neither side has a matching event, `windows` is `[]`.
782	- With `from`/`to`, only events in the closed interval
783	  `from <= occurredAt <= to` count, and **every** window intersecting that
784	  interval gets a row, including windows empty on both sides.
785	- Each row is `{"start", "leftCount", "rightCount", "equal"}`, with
786	  `equal` true exactly when the two counts agree.
787	- `decision.left` and `decision.right` each carry `peakStart`,
788	  `peakCount`, and `action`: the peak is the largest window count, ties
789	  resolve to the earliest window start, and `action` is `"escalate"` when
790	  the peak reaches `threshold` and `"observe"` otherwise. `decision.equal`
791	  is true exactly when the two sides' peak results agree. An empty side has
792	  `peakStart: null`, `peakCount: 0`, and `action: "observe"`.
793	
794	The `200` response is compact JSON with keys sorted by code point, integer
795	values kept as integers, booleans kept as booleans, and one trailing
796	newline:
797	
798	```json
799	{"decision":{"equal":false,"left":{"action":"observe","peakCount":2,"peakStart":0},"right":{"action":"escalate","peakCount":3,"peakStart":60}},"from":null,"left":"br-a","organizationId":"org-1","right":"br-b","threshold":3,"to":null,"type":"incident.created","windowSize":60,"windows":[{"equal":false,"leftCount":2,"rightCount":1,"start":0},{"equal":false,"leftCount":0,"rightCount":3,"start":60}]}
800	```
801	
802	```bash
803	curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/branches/compare \
804	  -H 'Authorization: Bearer tok-1' \
805	  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
806	  -d '{"organizationId":"org-1","left":"br-a","right":"br-b","type":"incident.created","windowSize":60,"threshold":3}'
807	```
808	
809	- `401 Unauthorized` — the Bearer credential is missing, malformed, or not
810	  registered.
811	- `403 Forbidden` (`{"error": "forbidden"}`) — the credential is bound to a
812	  different organization, or one of the named branches belongs to another
813	  organization. The organization decision happens before branch names are
814	  inspected, and branches are checked in the fixed order `left` then
815	  `right` (a missing left outranks any problem on the right).
816	- `404 Not Found` (`{"error": "branch_not_found"}`) — either `left` or
817	  `right` has never existed as a branch. Both participating branches must
818	  already exist; a comparison never implicitly creates a branch.
819	- `415 Unsupported Media Type` — missing or unsupported `Content-Type`.
820	- `400 Bad Request` — body is not syntactically valid JSON.
821	- `422 Unprocessable Entity` (`validation_error`) — a non-object body, a
822	  missing or extra field, a blank or non-string `organizationId`/`left`/
823	  `right`/`type`, non-positive-integer `windowSize`/`threshold`, unpaired or
824	  non-integer `from`/`to`, or `from > to`.
825	
826	Every non-`200` result is read-only as well: a failed comparison creates no
827	branch and changes no event, reservation, or decision state.

835	service is read for mutation or written, and identical submissions return

1052	- `422 Unprocessable Entity` (`validation_error`) — a non-object body, a
1053	  missing or extra field, or a blank or non-string
1054	  `organizationId`/`left`/`right`.
1055	
1056	Every non-`200` result is read-only as well: a failed comparison creates no
1057	branch and changes no event, reservation, alert, or main-service state.
1058	
1059	### `POST /snapshots/compare`
1060	
1061	A read-only comparison of two existing snapshots' window counts and peak
1062	decisions. Where `POST /branches/compare` recomputes over two branches'
1063	live events, this entry point recomputes over the events the two snapshots
1064	captured at their own creation times; nothing in either snapshot, in any
1065	branch, or in the main service is read for mutation or written — snapshots
1066	are immutable, the main-service event ledger, reservation inventory, and
1067	alert state are untouched, and identical submissions return byte-for-byte
1068	identical JSON. Both `read` and `write` credentials may call it. Requires
1069	`Content-Type: application/json` and a Bearer credential bound to the
1070	request's `organizationId`. The body must be a JSON object containing
1071	exactly these fields:
1072	
1073	| Field            | Rule                                                          |
1074	| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
1075	| `organizationId` | required, non-empty string; both snapshots must belong to it |
1076	| `left`           | required, non-empty snapshot name (the left-hand side)      |
1077	| `right`          | required, non-empty snapshot name (the right-hand side)     |
1078	| `type`           | required, non-empty string                                   |
1079	| `windowSize`     | required, positive integer (no booleans, floats, or strings) |
1080	| `threshold`      | required, positive integer (no booleans, floats, or strings) |
1081	| `from`           | optional; non-negative integer, present only together with `to` |
1082	| `to`             | optional; non-negative integer, present only together with `from` |
1083	
1084	Using the same snapshot name for `left` and `right` is legal; the two sides
1085	are then equal by construction. Window division matches the aggregate and
1086	decision entry points exactly: windows start at `0` and cover
1087	`[start, start + windowSize)`, and an event counts toward the window of
1088	`floor(occurredAt / windowSize) * windowSize`.
1089	
1090	- Without `from`/`to`, the `windows` rows cover the **union** of the windows
1091	  hit by matching captured events on either side, aligned row-by-row by
1092	  `start` ascending. A window hit by only one side shows the other side's
1093	  count as `0`. When neither side has a matching event, `windows` is `[]`.
1094	- With `from`/`to`, only events in the closed interval
1095	  `from <= occurredAt <= to` count, and **every** window intersecting that
1096	  interval gets a row, including windows empty on both sides.
1097	- Each row is `{"start", "leftCount", "rightCount", "equal"}`, with
1098	  `equal` true exactly when the two counts agree.
1099	- `decision.left` and `decision.right` each carry `peakStart`,
1100	  `peakCount`, and `action`: the peak is the largest window count, ties
1101	  resolve to the earliest window start, and `action` is `"escalate"` when
1102	  the peak reaches `threshold` and `"observe"` otherwise. `decision.equal`
1103	  is true exactly when the two sides' peak results agree. An empty side has
1104	  `peakStart: null`, `peakCount: 0`, and `action: "observe"`.
1105	
1106	The `200` response is compact JSON with keys sorted by code point, integer
1107	values kept as integers, booleans kept as booleans, and one trailing
1108	newline:
1109	
1110	```json
1111	{"decision":{"equal":false,"left":{"action":"observe","peakCount":2,"peakStart":0},"right":{"action":"escalate","peakCount":3,"peakStart":60}},"from":null,"left":"snap-a","organizationId":"org-1","right":"snap-b","threshold":3,"to":null,"type":"incident.created","windowSize":60,"windows":[{"equal":false,"leftCount":2,"rightCount":1,"start":0},{"equal":false,"leftCount":0,"rightCount":3,"start":60}]}
1112	```
1113	
1114	```bash
1115	curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/snapshots/compare \
1116	  -H 'Authorization: Bearer tok-1' \
1117	  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
1118	  -d '{"organizationId":"org-1","left":"snap-a","right":"snap-b","type":"incident.created","windowSize":60,"threshold":3}'
1119	```
1120	
1121	- `401 Unauthorized` — the Bearer credential is missing, malformed, or not
1122	  registered.
1123	- `403 Forbidden` (`{"error": "forbidden"}`) — the credential is bound to a
1124	  different organization, or one of the named snapshots belongs to another
1125	  organization. The organization decision happens before snapshot names are
1126	  inspected, and snapshots are checked in the fixed order `left` then
1127	  `right` (a missing left outranks any problem on the right).
1128	- `404 Not Found` (`{"error": "snapshot_not_found"}`) — either `left` or
1129	  `right` has never existed as a snapshot. Both participating snapshots
1130	  must already exist; a comparison never implicitly creates a snapshot.
1131	- `415 Unsupported Media Type` — missing or unsupported `Content-Type`.
1132	- `400 Bad Request` — body is not syntactically valid JSON.
1133	- `422 Unprocessable Entity` (`validation_error`) — a non-object body, a
1134	  missing or extra field, a blank or non-string `organizationId`/`left`/
1135	  `right`/`type`, non-positive-integer `windowSize`/`threshold`, unpaired or
1136	  non-integer `from`/`to`, or `from > to`.
1137	
1138	Every non-`200` result is read-only as well: a failed comparison creates no
1139	snapshot and changes no event, reservation, alert, or main-service state.
1140	
1141	### `POST /snapshots/compare/events`
1142	
1143	A read-only, event-level comparison of two existing snapshots. Where the
1144	branch comparison aligns two branches' live events, this entry point aligns
1145	the events the two snapshots captured at their own creation times, by
1146	`eventId`, and reports the deterministic difference summary. Nothing in
1147	either snapshot, in any branch, or in the main service is read for mutation
1148	or written — snapshots are immutable, the main-service event ledger,
1149	reservation inventory, and alert state are untouched, and identical
1150	submissions return byte-for-byte identical JSON. Both `read` and `write`
1151	credentials may call it. Requires `Content-Type: application/json` and a
1152	Bearer credential bound to the request's `organizationId`. The body must be
1153	a JSON object containing exactly these fields:
1154	
1155	| Field            | Rule                                                          |
1156	| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
1157	| `organizationId` | required, non-empty string; both snapshots must belong to it |
1158	| `left`           | required, non-empty snapshot name (the left-hand side)      |
1159	| `right`          | required, non-empty snapshot name (the right-hand side)     |
1160	
1161	Using the same snapshot name for `left` and `right` is legal; the two sides
1162	are then the same capture and every shared event lands in `same`.
1163	
1164	Events are aligned by `eventId`:
1165	
1166	- `leftOnly` — identifiers that appear only in the left snapshot.
1167	- `rightOnly` — identifiers that appear only in the right snapshot.
1168	- `same` — identifiers on both sides whose events are identical in every
1169	  field except `eventId`; payloads compare by content, so key order inside
1170	  a payload never matters.
1171	- `diff` — identifiers on both sides whose events disagree. Each entry is
1172	  `{"eventId", "fields"}`, where `fields` names the mismatched fields
1173	  (drawn from `organizationId`, `type`, `occurredAt`, `payload`).
1174	
1175	Identifiers and field names are sorted in Unicode code-point order. Each
1176	group array is accompanied by a count key named after the group plus
1177	`Count` (`leftOnlyCount`, `rightOnlyCount`, `sameCount`, `diffCount`). When
1178	neither snapshot holds any event, all four groups are empty arrays and all
1179	four counts are `0`.
1180	
1181	The `200` response is compact JSON with keys sorted by code point, integer
1182	values kept as integers, and one trailing newline:
1183	
1184	```json
1185	{"diff":[{"eventId":"evt-2","fields":["occurredAt","payload"]}],"diffCount":1,"leftOnly":["evt-1"],"leftOnlyCount":1,"rightOnly":["evt-4"],"rightOnlyCount":1,"same":["evt-3"],"sameCount":1}
1186	```
1187	
1188	```bash
1189	curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/snapshots/compare/events \
1190	  -H 'Authorization: Bearer tok-1' \
1191	  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
1192	  -d '{"organizationId":"org-1","left":"snap-a","right":"snap-b"}'
1193	```
1194	
1195	- `401 Unauthorized` — the Bearer credential is missing, malformed, or not
1196	  registered.
1197	- `403 Forbidden` (`{"error": "forbidden"}`) — the credential is bound to a
1198	  different organization, or one of the named snapshots belongs to another
1199	  organization. The organization decision happens before snapshot names are
1200	  inspected, and snapshots are checked in the fixed order `left` then
1201	  `right` (a missing left outranks any problem on the right).
1202	- `404 Not Found` (`{"error": "snapshot_not_found"}`) — either `left` or
1203	  `right` has never existed as a snapshot. Both participating snapshots
1204	  must already exist; a comparison never implicitly creates a snapshot.
1205	- `415 Unsupported Media Type` — missing or unsupported `Content-Type`.
1206	- `400 Bad Request` — body is not syntactically valid JSON.
1207	- `422 Unprocessable Entity` (`validation_error`) — a non-object body, a
1208	  missing or extra field, or a blank or non-string
1209	  `organizationId`/`left`/`right`.
1210	
1211	Every non-`200` result is read-only as well: a failed comparison creates no
1212	snapshot and changes no event, reservation, alert, or main-service state.

1224	`Content-Type: application/json` and a Bearer credential bound to the

1227

1229	| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |

1231	| `left`           | required, non-empty snapshot name (the left-hand side)      |
1232	| `right`          | required, non-empty snapshot name (the right-hand side)     |

1234	Using the same snapshot name for `left` and `right` is legal; the two sides
1235	are then the same capture and every shared reservation lands in `same`.

1237	Reservations are aligned by `reservationId`:
1238	
1239	- `leftOnly` — identifiers that appear only in the left snapshot.
1240	- `rightOnly` — identifiers that appear only in the right snapshot.
1241	- `same` — identifiers on both sides whose `organizationId`, `resourceId`,
1242	  `quantity`, and `capacity` all match.
1243	- `diff` — identifiers on both sides that disagree in at least one of those
1244	  four fields. Each entry is `{"reservationId", "fields"}`, where `fields`
1245	  names the mismatched fields, drawn only from `organizationId`,
1246	  `resourceId`, `quantity`, and `capacity`; no other content participates
1247	  in the comparison.

1252	neither snapshot holds any reservation for the organization, all four

1260	```
1261	
1262	```bash
1263	curl -X POST http://127.0.0.1:8000/snapshots/compare/reservations \
1264	  -H 'Authorization: Bearer tok-1' \
1265	  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
1266	  -d '{"organizationId":"org-1","left":"snap-a","right":"snap-b"}'
1267	```

1270	  registered.
1271	- `403 Forbidden` (`{"error": "forbidden"}`) — the credential is bound to a

1273	  organization. The organization decision happens before snapshot names are

1283	  `organizationId`/`left`/`right`.
1284	
1285	Every non-`200` result is read-only as well: a failed comparison creates no

1288	### `POST /snapshots/compare/resources`

1291	`POST /snapshots/compare/reservations` aligns captured reservations by
1292	`reservationId`, this entry point aligns the resources the two snapshots
1293	captured at their own creation times, by `resourceId`, and compares the two
1294	sides' three resource balances — `capacity`, `occupied`, and `remaining`.
1295	Nothing in either snapshot, in any branch, or in the main service is read
1296	for mutation or written — snapshots are immutable, alert state is untouched,
1297	and identical submissions return byte-for-byte identical JSON. Both `read`
1298	and `write` credentials may call it. Requires `Content-Type:
1299	application/json` and a Bearer credential bound to the request's
1300	`organizationId`. The body must be a JSON object containing exactly these
1301	fields:
1302	
1303	| Field            | Rule                                                          |
1304	| ---------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
1305	| `organizationId` | required, non-empty string; both snapshots must belong to it |
1306	| `left`           | required, non-empty snapshot name (the left-hand side)      |
1307	| `right`          | required, non-empty snapshot name (the right-hand side)     |
